category: mathematical logic / computability and Diophantine definability
literal_source_claim: Recursively enumerable sets are Diophantine sets.
canonical_claim: For every finite arity, every recursively enumerable subset of the corresponding natural-number tuples is Diophantine.
domain_and_universes: Intended finite powers of Nat; exact choice among Fin n -> Nat, Vector, or a coded Nat input and the universe of witness indices remains open.
quantifiers: for every finite input arity n
for every subset S of Nat^n
if S is recursively enumerable under the source-selected definition
then there exist finitely many witness variables and an integer polynomial representing membership in S
hypotheses: S is recursively enumerable; the exact Lean predicate and tuple coding must be selected from an immutable source crosswalk
conclusion: S is Diophantine with natural-number witnesses and an integer-coefficient polynomial, after checked transport to mathlib's Dioph encoding.
excluded_degenerate_cases: Arity zero, empty/full sets, zero witness arity, Nat versus Int solutions, single-polynomial versus finite-system presentations, and uniform versus per-arity formulations are not excluded; their exact treatment must be frozen at statement phase.
